title: Rolle der Farben
slide_intent: Separate identity from functional signals so viewers can recognize both the organization and the service context.
strategic_value: Stable assignments can help DB preserve brand recognition while distinguishing wayfinding, replacement service and service communication.
demonstration: The section explains brand-identity colors before presenting DB Red and function-specific blue, purple and service-red swatches.
practical_value: Check whether the color is identifying a brand or signaling a service function before applying it.

content_islands.name: Role introduction
content_islands.spec: Explain consistent communication and list DB Red and S-Bahn Green as brand-identity colors.

content_islands.name: Brand specimen
content_islands.spec: Present the DB Red values beneath its role statement; retain the source’s S-Bahn label where its separate specimen is absent.

content_islands.name: Functional colors
content_islands.spec: Group wayfinding blue, replacement-service purple and service red with their intended uses.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text links color roles to recognition, orientation and differentiation.
reference_purposes.Application: The functional assignments connect named colors to specific communication contexts.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source says brand-identity colors occur at least once in a layout.

ingredient.name: Identity and functional colors
ingredient.role: Distinguish the sender from the service being communicated.
ingredient.application: Use the relevant identity color at least once and preserve the specified functional color assignments.
ingredient.scope: The section distinguishes DB and S-Bahn identities; it does not require both identity colors in every DB layout.
